messages:
Anna (support): Hey @mobile-team, ACME reported repeated mid-stream disconnects when a phone switches from carrier -> Android hotspot. They see partial SSE output then the client closes. Repro attached, can someone triage?
Diego (sre): Can you paste the raw curl and any proxy logs? Sounds like NAT/pinhole timeout or hotspot NAT remap.
Anna (support): Repro curl:
```
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-4o" \
  --compressed
```
Client is on Pixel 6, start on mobile data, enable tethering, switch client to hotspot. After ~10-15s we see partial events then client-side close (499). Backend shows generation continued for ~8s after FIN.
Kim (mobile): Android hotspot often changes NAT mapping and causes TCP reset. Does our SDK use SSE Last-Event-ID resume? If not, client can't resume. Also token TTL race can cause reconnect 401s.
Jules (customer-success): Customer is worried about partial outputs and billing. If they reconnect and see duplicate tokens or partial content, they want a predictable UX.
Priya (eng-runtime): We do send an `id:` line per event, but we don't currently persist output for reconnect/resume — runtime keeps per-connection state only. Resuming from Last-Event-ID would require short-lived buffering keyed by event-id. Token TTL on their setup is 30s which won't survive some reconnects.
Diego (sre): From edge logs: request req_0abc from IP 198.51.100.23 -> proxy edge-pool-3. Sequence: SYN/ACK then keepalive idle, then FIN when NAT remap occurs. Proxy returned 499 (client closed) while backend still running; proxy keepalive timeout configured to 10s on that pool.
Anna (support): Repro steps I gave to customer: 1) Start stream on mobile data 2) Turn on phone hotspot and tether client 3) Watch partial chunks then disconnect 4) Reconnect immediately -> sometimes 401 or new session (no resume).
Kim (mobile): We'll push SDK changes: keep local event-id, on reconnect send Last-Event-ID header and attempt resume. Also prefetch token refresh before hot-swap; fallback to 3x auto-retries with exponential backoff.
Priya (eng-runtime): Short term we can: a) increase proxy keepalive to 30s for affected edge-pool, b) add explicit debug log when Last-Event-ID present, c) emit a final `event: eos` on graceful completes. Long-term: evaluate per-request ephemeral buffer to allow resume within N seconds (design ticket).
Diego (sre): Actioned: raised keepalive to 30s for edge-pool-3 (rolling 10% now). Added trace logs for Last-Event-ID header on reconnect attempts.
OpsBot: deploy queued: edge-pool-3 keepalive update -> rollout started (10%) :rocket:
Priya (eng-runtime): Filed infra ticket INF-1423 to spike ephemeral buffer for resume; ENG-950 to track resumable-stream feature. No ETA yet, spike this week.
Jules (customer-success): Billing: flagged to finance — is partial output billed? Current policy bills generated tokens; we'll ask finance for an exception/clarification for obvious network-abort cases.
Anna (support): Workaround provided to ACME: use SDK dev build with resume + token prefetch, set client keepalive pings every 10s, and ensure token TTL >= 120s before switching network. Also we recommended they enable client-side buffering to dedupe partials.
Diego (sre): I'll follow up in 24h with logs and monitor the rollout. If we still see 499 patterns after keepalive change we'll open a higher-priority incident.
Kim (mobile): I'll open the SDK PR and tag QA for hotspot repro.
Priya (eng-runtime): Quick note: adding an 'eos' sentinel is low-risk and we'll push that first. Resume buffer requires sizing decisions (memory vs TTL).
Anna (support): Thanks all — I'll update ACME and leave this thread open for updates.
